chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ibn Rabat and Al-Husayn ibn Hashim from Safwan, all from Ibn Muskan from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the divorce of the intoxicated one, so he said: It is not valid, nor is his emancipation (of a slave).
ai.seo_question: Is the divorce of an intoxicated person valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the divorce of an intoxicated person is valid (*ja'iz*) and their emancipation of a slave is also valid (*'itq*), establishing that intoxication does not nullify legal capacity (*ahliyyah*) for these specific acts. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between the state of intoxication and insanity, affirming that voluntary intoxication does not invalidate contractual obligations or family law actions. The consensus among scholars is that since the person is still conscious and aware, their declarations hold legal weight without needing re-confirmation.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Ibn Rabat and Al Husayn Bin Hashim, from Safwan, altogether from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a divorce by the intoxicated one, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Not allowed, nor his emancipation (liberation of a slave)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from ibn Ribat and al-Husayn ibn Hashim from Safwan all from ibn Muskan from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the divorce of a drunken man. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not permissible as well as his setting free of slaves.’”
